title: Security, National Interest, and Transnational Actors

scenes.text: Is national security about borders, or protecting human lives?
scenes.narration: When you hear the word security, do you only think of tanks and soldiers at borders? Today, we will explore why modern security goes far deeper than military defence alone.

scenes.text: A gated society with armed guards, yet contaminated drinking water inside.
scenes.narration: Here is an analogy: imagine a gated housing society with armed guards at the gate. The boundary is secure, but inside, families fall sick from polluted water. True security protects life inside the gates too.

scenes.name: Cynthia Enloe
scenes.idea: State security perspectives are heavily gendered, neglecting everyday human security.
scenes.narration: Thinker Cynthia Enloe explains that traditional security views are heavily gendered. States prioritise weapons and borders, while neglecting the everyday safety, health, and dignity of human beings.

scenes.heading: Buzan's Comprehensive Security Model
scenes.narration: Copenhagen school scholar Barry Buzan shows that security must be comprehensive. At the centre sits human security, expanding outward to national and global levels across military, ecological, and economic pillars.

scenes.heading: National Interest Debate
scenes.narration: Here's the trick with national interest: is it real or a pseudo-theory? Raymond Aron called it vague, while Mohammad Yunus showed how Pakistan's army presents its institutional interests as the nation's interest.

scenes.heading: Perspectives on Transnational Actors
scenes.narration: Who shapes world politics today? Realists see non-state actors merely as state proxies, liberals welcome them as engines of development, while Marxists view corporations as tools of exploitation.

scenes.heading: Rise of Transnational Power
scenes.narration: Joseph Nye introduced the three-dimensional chessboard model to explain how power diffuses. Globalisation, the internet revolution, and human rights awareness have empowered non-state actors worldwide.

items: Security expands beyond borders to human lives
National interest is often shaped by elites
Transnational actors diffuse power across the globe
scenes.narration: Remember these three big ideas: true security protects human lives, national interest can be subjective, and transnational actors now share the global chessboard.
